title: Compilers
tagline: Lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, data-flow analysis and optimisation, code generation, register allocation and runtime systems
summary: A compiler translates programs into machine code that runs fast, and its techniques power many other tools, from linters to query engines. This course follows a program through the phases of a compiler — lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, data-flow analysis and optimisation, instruction selection and register allocation — and ends with runtime systems and garbage collection.

chapters.title: The structure of a compiler
chapters.summary: Phases and passes, front and back ends, and bootstrapping.

chapters.title: Lexical analysis
chapters.summary: Tokens, regular expressions and generating scanners from finite automata.

chapters.title: Top-down parsing
chapters.summary: Recursive descent, FIRST and FOLLOW sets, and LL(1) parsing.

chapters.title: Bottom-up parsing
chapters.summary: Shift–reduce parsing, LR(0), SLR, LR(1) and LALR parsers, and parser generators.

chapters.title: Semantic analysis
chapters.summary: Abstract syntax trees, symbol tables, scope resolution and type checking.

chapters.title: Intermediate representations
chapters.summary: Three-address code, control-flow graphs and static single assignment form.

chapters.title: Data-flow analysis and optimisation
chapters.summary: Liveness and reaching definitions, lattices and fixed points, and classic optimisations.

chapters.title: Code generation and register allocation
chapters.summary: Instruction selection, calling conventions, and register allocation by graph colouring.

chapters.title: Runtime systems and garbage collection
chapters.summary: Activation records, objects and closures at run time, and garbage-collection algorithms.
